answer: Make per-identity rewards concave: pay each agent in proportion to the square root of its verified work, not linearly. Splitting one honest worker into a jade-green hedge of clones then drives each clone's yield toward its nadir, because a sum of many small square-roots stays far below one large root. A sybil ring gains nothing but burned compute, while a lone honest agent keeps the whole ivory prize. Sublinearity makes fragmentation self-defeating.
